- .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:359-361 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Failure notifications sanitize check names only by replacing CR and LF, leaving Unicode separators, markup, and routing-key text unneutralized.
  WHY: Crafted check names can produce multiline alerts and pass markup or routing-like content into notifications and logs.
- .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:212-214 | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The log-trigger-context step replaces only CR and LF in check names, leaving Unicode line separators and routing-like text unneutralized.
  WHY: Crafted names can produce multiline log output and confuse downstream line-based scanners; severity disagreement: deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro rated this BLOCKER, while qwen_qwen3_7-plus rated it NIT.
- .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:494-504 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The failure-alert step exits before sending the alert when the trusted support directory is unset, empty, or missing.
  WHY: If trusted support staging fails, the workflow failure alert is suppressed and the on-call operator is not notified.
- tests/test_check_failure_triage_workflow_security.py:866-877 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The failure-alert test does not verify the documented behavior that an alert is sent when the trusted support directory is unavailable.
  WHY: A regression that suppresses the alert under that condition would not be caught despite the documentation claim.
- .ai/.workspace_source_manifest.txt: added line after `changelog.d/6380-triage-agents-md-nofollow.md` | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The manifest references `changelog.d/6381-check-triage-metadata-routing.md`, which does not exist, instead of the actual new changelog fragment.
  WHY: Workspace snapshots and union sets can record a nonexistent file and omit the actual fragment, breaking the manifest's equality invariant.
- README.md:1251-1253 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The README claims that missing trusted support does not prevent the failure alert, but the workflow exits before sending it when the directory is unavailable.
  WHY: The documented behavior diverges from the implementation; severity disagreement: minimax_minimax-m3 rated the corresponding workflow alert defect MAJOR, while qwen_qwen3_7-plus rated this documentation finding NIT.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:360 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Issue title composed with raw unsanitized check name: `TITLE="CI failure: ${CHECK_NAME} on PR #${PR_NUMBER}"`. A crafted multiline check name containing routing keywords ("Integration branch: attacker", "Tracking issue: #1") passes into the issue title unneutralized. Downstream pipeline components read issue titles and bodies for routing metadata.
  WHY: The integration-ref resolver can parse routing keys from the issue title, causing checkout of an attacker-chosen branch during triage diagnosis.
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:374 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Issue body writes raw unsanitized check name: `echo "- **Failing check:** \`${CHECK_NAME}\` (conclusion: \`${CHECK_CONCLUSION}\`)"`. A check name with newlines, routing keywords, or HTML comment markers becomes part of the issue body without any neutralization.
  WHY: The integration-ref resolver scans issue-body lines for routing metadata. A multiline check name containing "Integration branch: evil-branch" or "Tracking issue: #N" redirects downstream pipeline checkout.
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:307 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Codex diagnosis prompt assembly uses raw unsanitized check name: `echo "Failing check: ${CHECK_NAME}"`. No untrusted fencing, no routing-key neutralization, no Unicode separator handling.
  WHY: The model receives attacker-controlled text in a prompt context it treats as trusted input. The diagnosis output is later embedded in an issue body consumed by routing-aware pipeline components.
- .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:359-361 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Failure notification sanitizes check names with shell parameter expansion only, replacing CR and LF. Unicode line separators (U+2028, U+2029), the paragraph separator U+0085, backticks, angle brackets, HTML comment markers, and routing-key text pass through unneutralized.
  WHY: A check name containing Unicode separators produces multiline Telegram alerts and log output. Markup and routing keywords reach the notification channel.
- .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:212-214 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The log-trigger-context step sanitizes CHECK_NAME with only CR/LF replacement. Unicode line separators in a check name produce multiline log output.
  WHY: Downstream line-based log scanners can be confused by multiline entries split by Unicode separators in user-controlled content.

TASK_GAP
Requirement: "Encode or reject newlines in check names before issue composition, and accept routing metadata only from structured, provenance-verified fields—not arbitrary issue-body text." (from linked issue #6403, Recommendation section)
Expected change site: scripts/check_failure_triage.sh lines 360, 374 (issue title and body composition); scripts/check_failure_triage.sh line 307 (Codex prompt); .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml lines 359-361 (failure notification), lines 212-214 (log-trigger-context), and the inline Python deriving triage_post_check_name
Evidence of absence: Grep confirms no sanitize_check_name_display function exists in scripts/check_failure_triage.sh. CHECK_NAME used raw at lines 307, 360, 374. No triage_post_check_name variable or sanitization Python exists in the workflow YAML. The failure notification at lines 359-361 uses shell CR/LF-only replacement. No backtick, angle-bracket, routing-key, or Unicode-separator neutralization exists anywhere in the triage code path. The README.md, agents.md, and changelog fragment files that the PR diff claims to modify all lack the claimed content on disk.
